title: The controller cannot open new device sessions
scenario: The controller at 10.10.5.20 can ping SW3 10.10.0.13 but its new SSH connections time out. Users through SW3 still work. A console inspection confirms this ACL is applied inbound to every usable VTY range. These are authored diagnostic excerpts.

exhibits.title: SW3 VTY configuration
exhibits.text:
line vty 0 15
 access-class MGMT-IN in
 login local
 transport input ssh

exhibits.title: SW3 management ACL
exhibits.text:
Standard IP access list MGMT-IN
 10 permit 10.10.99.0 0.0.0.255
 20 deny any

question: Which mismatch is established by the configuration?
options: The controller source is excluded from the device's VTY permit list
The SSH user is explicitly rejected after password authentication
The switch's transit ACL blocks all user traffic through the switch
The controller has no ICMP route to the switch management address
explanation: 10.10.5.20 does not match the only permit and reaches deny any for VTY access. A VTY access-class does not apply to ordinary transit frames or prove that other management protocols are also blocked. The supplied source and ACL establish the SSH mismatch without attributing unrelated counters.
fix:
```ios
SW3# configure terminal
SW3(config)# ip access-list standard MGMT-IN
SW3(config-std-nacl)# 15 permit host 10.10.5.20
SW3(config-std-nacl)# end
SW3# show access-lists MGMT-IN
```
Retest a new SSH session from the controller's actual source and then its documented synchronization workflow.
Repeat a user-service test through SW3 as well. A controller synchronization result and preserved client forwarding are separate acceptance observations.

title: A replacement path passes small tests but stalls larger traffic
scenario: A controlled VXLAN design carries a 1500-byte inner IP packet with 14 bytes inner Ethernet, 8 VXLAN, 8 UDP and 20 outer IPv4 bytes. No inner VLAN tag is retained. A replacement underlay interface has an effective IP MTU of 1500. The design requires an outer IP MTU of at least 1550 along this path.

exhibits.title: Representative path evidence
exhibits.text:
Small endpoint-locator ICMP tests: successful
1550-byte outer IPv4 test with DF: ICMP fragmentation-needed received
Reported next-hop MTU: 1500
Replacement interface effective IP MTU: 1500
Other tested path interfaces: effective IP MTU at least 1550

question: What established issue should the approved repair address?
options: The approved overlay identifier is mismatched at the two tunnel endpoints
The return route is absent for packets of every tested size
The replacement interface cannot carry the required outer IP packet
The controller's stored inventory is too old to authenticate the application
explanation: The required outer IP packet is 1500+14+8+8+20=1550 bytes. Explicit fragmentation-needed evidence and the replacement interface's effective MTU establish the size mismatch. This is stronger than inferring MTU solely from a stalled file copy.
fix: Use the replacement platform's documented MTU procedure to meet the approved end-to-end design, checking whether a reload or interface action is required. Do not blindly apply a system-wide command to an unspecified model. Recheck the effective MTU, repeat the 1550-byte DF test, and test the actual application and return direction.
